title: thigh (anterior, lateral, medial and posterior)

chart.description: The thigh unrolled round the whole limb, from the inguinal crease and the gluteal fold to the knee. u: distance round the limb (cm) from the anterior line of the thigh (the line from the femoral pulse at the mid-inguinal point to the middle of the patella), positive towards lateral, negative towards medial. The back of the thigh is reached round the LATERAL side: the lateral midline (iliotibial band) lies at u = +10 to +14 and the posterior midline at about u = +27 at the gluteal fold, narrowing to +18.5 at the popliteal crease as the thigh tapers; the medial thigh (sartorius, gracilis, the adductors) is reached round the medial side (u = -8 to -12). v: distance along the limb (cm) from the midpoint of the base of the patella with the knee extended, positive cranial. d: depth below the skin (cm). Offsets keep the chart's sense: 'lateral' is further round the lateral side (on the back of the thigh: towards the posterior midline), 'medial' further round the medial side.

configurations.label: hip and knee extended (lying supine or prone)
knee flexed (seated, supine with a bolster under the knee, or side-lying with hips and knees flexed): the patella lies about 2 cm lower on the femur

landmarks.label: anterior superior iliac spine
landmarks.palpation: The bony point at the front end of the iliac crest.

landmarks.label: upper border of the pubic symphysis (in the anterior median line)
landmarks.palpation: Slide down the midline of the lower abdomen until the finger meets the upper edge of the pubic bones.

landmarks.label: femoral pulse at the inguinal crease (mid-inguinal point)
landmarks.palpation: Supine, the strongest pulsation just below the middle of the inguinal ligament.

landmarks.label: site of ST30: the groin at the level of the upper border of the pubic symphysis, 2 B-cun lateral to the anterior median line, over the femoral vessels
landmarks.palpation: Level with the upper border of the pubic symphysis, 2 B-cun lateral to the midline; the femoral pulse is felt just below and lateral to it.

landmarks.label: site of SP12: on the inguinal crease, just lateral to the femoral pulse
landmarks.palpation: Feel the femoral pulse at the inguinal crease; SP12 lies on the crease just lateral to it.

landmarks.label: depression below the anterior superior iliac spine between sartorius, tensor fasciae latae and the proximal rectus femoris
landmarks.palpation: Ask the patient to lift the straight leg slightly: below the ASIS the sartorius (medial) and tensor fasciae latae (lateral) form a V; the hollow at its apex, over the proximal rectus femoris, lies on the line from the ASIS to the lateral end of the base of the patella, about level with the lower border of the pubic symphysis.

landmarks.label: prominence of the greater trochanter
landmarks.palpation: The broad bony prominence on the side of the hip; it rolls under the fingers when the thigh is rotated.

landmarks.label: midpoint of the gluteal fold
landmarks.palpation: Prone: the middle of the transverse fold below the buttock.

landmarks.label: midpoint of the popliteal crease
landmarks.palpation: Prone: the middle of the transverse crease at the back of the knee.

landmarks.label: lateral end of the popliteal crease, at the medial border of the biceps femoris tendon
landmarks.palpation: Flex the knee against resistance: the biceps femoris tendon stands out at the lateral side of the back of the knee; the crease ends at its medial border.

landmarks.label: midpoint of the superior border (base) of the patella
landmarks.palpation: The upper border of the patella, at its middle.

landmarks.label: lateral end of the base of the patella
landmarks.palpation: The upper outer corner of the patella.

landmarks.label: medial end of the base of the patella
landmarks.palpation: The upper inner corner of the patella.

landmarks.label: medial epicondyle of the femur
landmarks.palpation: The most prominent point on the inner side of the lower femur, just above the knee joint line.

landmarks.label: lateral epicondyle of the femur
landmarks.palpation: The most prominent point on the outer side of the lower femur, above the joint line.

segments.label: upper border of the pubic symphysis to the medial epicondyle of the femur

source.title: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (2008): proportional bone measurement, lower limb
source.note: Used for the anterior and medial thigh (ST, SP, LR channels and the extra points above the patella).

segments.label: prominence of the greater trochanter to the popliteal crease (lateral end)

source.title: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (2008): proportional bone measurement, lower limb
source.note: Used for the lateral thigh (GB channel). The lateral end of the crease stands in for its level on this chart.

segments.label: gluteal fold to the popliteal crease (their midpoints)

source.title: WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (2008): proportional bone measurement, lower limb
source.note: Used for the posterior thigh (BL channel). The chart line between the two midpoints is about 3 % longer than the limb's length because the posterior midline moves round the tapering thigh.

layers.label: rectus femoris, sartorius and tensor fasciae latae
neck and upper shaft of the femur
femoral sheath and inguinal lymph nodes
adductor canal: femoral vessels and saphenous nerve
vastus medialis and the adductor magnus tendon
vastus lateralis beside the rectus femoris tendon
vastus lateralis and the short head of biceps femoris
hamstrings: biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus
lower border of gluteus maximus and the hamstring origins

structures.label: femoral artery (femoral triangle and adductor canal)
femoral vein (medial to the artery, then behind it)
femoral nerve (lateral to the artery, branching in the femoral triangle)
saphenous nerve (with the femoral artery in the adductor canal, then between sartorius and gracilis)
great saphenous vein (medial thigh to the saphenous opening)
lateral circumflex femoral artery (deep to rectus femoris)
sciatic nerve (deep in the posterior thigh)
tibial nerve (from the division of the sciatic nerve)
common fibular (peroneal) nerve along the biceps femoris
suprapatellar recess of the knee joint (deep to the quadriceps)

description: The thigh. In front, the femoral triangle lies below the inguinal ligament between sartorius and adductor longus; it holds, from lateral to medial, the femoral nerve, the femoral artery and the femoral vein, with the great saphenous vein entering the femoral vein at the saphenous opening; the deep femoral artery leaves the femoral artery a few centimetres below the ligament and runs deep. From the apex of the triangle the femoral artery and vein and the saphenous nerve pass under sartorius in the adductor canal and through the adductor hiatus to the back of the knee. The quadriceps covers the front of the femur; above the patella the suprapatellar recess of the knee joint lies deep to the quadriceps tendon. Laterally the iliotibial band runs from the greater trochanter towards the knee; the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve crosses the front of the upper thigh superficially. Behind, the hamstrings cover the sciatic nerve, which runs from the middle of the gluteal fold down the back of the thigh and divides above the knee into the tibial and common fibular nerves.

sources.title: General regional anatomy of the thigh and femoral triangle (standard anatomy texts)
sources.note: Topography only; no third-party geometry or images were used.

review.notes: Positions and depths are illustrative approximations of a reference adult written for simulation. They are not measurements or an atlas and are not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.
